questions.question_text:
The dot plot shows fern heights.
What is the range?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.8]
\draw[->] (-0.5,0)--(8.8,0); \foreach \x in {0,...,8} {\node[below,font=\scriptsize] at (\x,0) {$\x$};} \foreach \x/\c in {1/1,2/2,4/4,6/2,8/1} {\foreach \k in {1,...,\c} {\fill (\x,{0.34*\k}) circle (2.2pt);}} \node[below] at (4.5,-0.9) {Height (cm)};
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.text: $7$ cm
$8$ cm
options.why: Uses the largest value as the range instead of subtracting the smallest value.

options.text: $4$ cm
options.why: Gives the modal value rather than the difference between maximum and minimum.

options.text: $5$ cm
options.why: Counts the five occupied value positions instead of calculating maximum minus minimum.

questions.question_text:
The dot plot shows petals on flowers.
What is the mode?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.8]
\draw[->] (-0.5,0)--(8.8,0); \foreach \x in {0,...,8} {\node[below,font=\scriptsize] at (\x,0) {$\x$};} \foreach \x/\c in {2/1,3/3,4/2,6/5,7/2,8/1} {\foreach \k in {1,...,\c} {\fill (\x,{0.34*\k}) circle (2.2pt);}} \node[below] at (5,-0.9) {Number of petals};
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: Counts the dots in the tallest stack but gives the frequency instead of its value.
Uses the greatest data value instead of the value occurring most often.
Chooses the second-tallest stack rather than the tallest stack.

questions.solution_text: The tallest stack is above $6$, so the mode is $6$.

options.text: Trial B's range is $4$ mm greater
Trial A's range is $4$ mm greater
options.why: Reverses the comparison after finding ranges $4$ and $8$.

options.text: Both ranges are $8$ mm
options.why: Uses Trial B's maximum as the range for both displays.

options.text: Both ranges are $4$ mm
options.why: Uses Trial A's range for both displays and ignores Trial B's wider endpoints.

questions.solution_text:
Trial A: $6-2=4$ mm
Trial B: $8-0=8$ mm
$8-4=4$ mm
Trial B's range is $4$ mm greater.

options.text: Batch C has mode $2$ and Batch D has mode $5$
Batch C has mode $4$ and Batch D has mode $4$
options.why: Uses the frequencies of the tallest stacks instead of the values beneath them.

options.text: Batch C has mode $6$ and Batch D has mode $7$
options.why: Uses each dataset's largest value instead of its most frequent value.

options.text: Neither batch has a mode
options.why: Ignores that one value in each display has a uniquely tallest stack.

questions.solution_text: Batch C's tallest stack is at $2$; Batch D's tallest stack is at $5$.

questions.question_text:
The two displays have the same mode.
Which statement about their ranges is also true?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.78]
\draw[->] (-0.5,0)--(8.8,0); \draw[->] (-0.5,2.3)--(8.8,2.3); \foreach \x in {0,...,8} {\node[below,font=\scriptsize] at (\x,0) {$\x$}; \node[below,font=\scriptsize] at (\x,2.3) {$\x$};} \foreach \x/\c in {2/1,3/2,4/4,5/2,6/1} {\foreach \k in {1,...,\c} {\fill (\x,{0.32*\k}) circle (2.2pt);}} \foreach \x/\c in {1/1,2/2,4/5,7/2,8/1} {\foreach \k in {1,...,\c} {\fill (\x,{2.3+0.32*\k}) circle (2.2pt);}} \node[left] at (-0.55,0.8) {Patch E}; \node[left] at (-0.55,3.1) {Patch F}; \node[below] at (4.5,-0.9) {Plant height (cm)};
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.text: Patch F's range is $3$ cm greater
Patch E's range is $3$ cm greater
options.why: Finds the correct difference $7-4=3$ but reverses which patch is the more spread out one.

options.text: Patch F's range is $2$ cm greater
options.why: Compares only the maximum heights, $8-6=2$, instead of comparing the two ranges.

options.text: Patch E's range is $2$ cm greater
options.why: Compares only the maximum heights and subtracts them in the wrong order, $6-8$, reading it as $2$ cm in Patch E's favour.

questions.solution_text:
Patch E: $6-2=4$ cm
Patch F: $8-1=7$ cm
$7-4=3$ cm
Patch F's range is $3$ cm greater.

options.text: Both ranges are $7$; Batch A has mode $6$ and Batch B has mode $5$.
Batch A has range $9$ and Batch B has range $8$; their modes are $6$ and $5$, respectively.
options.why: Uses each largest value as the range instead of subtracting the smallest value.

options.text: Both ranges are $7$ and both modes are $4$.
options.why: Calculates the ranges correctly but gives the frequency of each tallest stack, $4$, instead of its data value.

options.text: Both ranges are $7$; Batch A has mode $9$ and Batch B has mode $8$.
options.why: Calculates the ranges correctly but uses each largest data value as its mode.

questions.solution_text:
Batch A range: $9-2=7$; mode: $6$.
Batch B range: $8-1=7$; mode: $5$.
The ranges are equal, and Batch A has the larger mode.

questions.question_text:
The test scores of students in Class 1 have a range of $26$.
The test scores of students in Class 2 have a range of $34$.
This means that…

options.text: The test scores of students in Class 1 are less consistent
options.why: A larger range, not a smaller one, indicates greater spread and less consistency.

options.text: Students in Class 1 had better test scores on average
options.why: Range gives no information about which class has the higher mean.

options.text: The test scores of students in Class 1 are more consistent
Students in Class 2 had better test scores on average
options.why: Range compares spread and cannot determine average performance.

questions.solution_text: Range measures the distance between the largest and smallest score. Class 1 has the smaller range, $26$ compared with $34$, so its scores are more consistent. The ranges do not determine either class mean.

questions.question_text:
By calculating the range of each data set, decide which set shows the greatest variability.
A: 23, 35, 42, 39, 27
B: 0, 11, 16, 3, 21
C: 4, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6, 6, 7, 7
D: 43, 43, 43, 43, 43

options.text: A
options.why: Its range is 19, which is less than B's range.

options.text: B
C
options.why: Its range is only 3, so the data vary less.

options.text: D
options.why: All values are equal, giving a range of zero.

questions.solution_text:
A: $42 - 23 = 19$
B: $21 - 0 = 21$
C: $7 - 4 = 3$
D: $43 - 43 = 0$
The greatest range is $21$, so B shows the greatest variability.
